---
title: "Regulatory crosswalk"
---

The model documentation follows the order of the US guidance, **SR 11-7** (Federal Reserve,
with the OCC's identical **OCC 2011-12**). This table maps each element to where it is
documented here and to the corresponding principles of **OSFI Guideline E-23**, *Model Risk
Management* (Canada, effective 1 May 2027) and **PRA SS1/23**, *Model risk management
principles for banks* (UK).

| SR 11-7 element | Here | OSFI E-23 | PRA SS1/23 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model definition and inventory | [D0](../mdd/d0-summary.qmd) | 2.1 (identify and track all models); the definition of a model | 1.1 (model definition), 1.2 (model inventory) |
| Purpose and use | [D1](../mdd/d1-purpose.qmd), N.1 | 1.3 (models appropriate for their business purposes) | 3.1 (model purpose and design); 5.2 (restrictions on model use) |
| Data | [D2](../mdd/d2-data.qmd), N.2 | 3.2 (data suitable for the intended use) | 3.2 (the use of data) |
| Model dependencies | [D3](../mdd/d3-dependencies.qmd) | model dependencies, among the inventory's data elements (Appendix 1) | 1.2 (inventory identifies model inter-dependencies) |
| Conceptual soundness | N.3, N.4 | 3.3 (development standards); 3.4 (independent assessment of conceptual soundness) | 3.1 (model purpose and design); 3.5 (model development documentation); 4.2 (independent review) |
| Implementation | [D9](../mdd/d9-implementation.qmd) | 3.5 (deployment with quality and change control) | 3.6 (supporting systems); 4.3 (process verification) |
| Performance and outcomes analysis | N.5 | 3.3 (standards for performance); 3.4 (reasonableness of model outcomes) | 3.3 (model development testing, including challenger models) |
| Sensitivity | N.6 | performance testing under development standards (3.3); the guideline does not name sensitivity analysis | 3.3 (sensitivity analysis to set operating boundaries); 4.4 (sensitivity testing in monitoring) |
| Limitations | N.7 | 3.4 (limitations and mitigants in review; approval with compensating mitigants) | 3.5 (documentation of assumptions and limitations); 5.1 (post-model adjustments) |
| Ongoing monitoring | N.8 | 3.6 (monitoring standards and thresholds for breaches) | 4.4 (model performance monitoring); 4.5 (periodic revalidation) |
| Governance and change control | [D9](../mdd/d9-implementation.qmd), N.9, D11 (validation PDF) | 1.1 (reporting structures and resourcing); 3.1 (policies across the lifecycle); 3.5 (approval hierarchies, change control) | 2.1–2.4 (board, SMF accountability, policies, roles); 5.3 (exceptions and escalations) |
| Risk tiering | [D0](../mdd/d0-summary.qmd) | 2.2 (model risk rating); 2.3 (intensity commensurate with risk) | 1.3 (model tiering) |
| AI/ML: explainability, autonomy, agent use | N.3, [D10](../mdd/d10-agents.qmd) | 3.3 (explainability requirements); 3.4 (explainability in review); 3.6 (autonomous decision-making in monitoring) | 1.3 (interpretability and explainability in tiering); 3.3 (models that change autonomously) |

N.1 to N.9 are the nine parts of every model chapter (D4 to D8); see
[the template](../mdd/index.qmd#the-template). D11, the sign-off, appears only in the
validation PDF.

## How this table was made

Principle numbers were read from the source documents, not from summaries: OSFI's
published E-23 guideline (the 2027 version) and the PRA's SS1/23 as published with PS6/23 in
May 2023. The PRA has since updated SS1/23; the sub-principle numbering above is that of
the 2023 text. Where E-23 has no principle that names a topic, the row says so and names the
closest expectation instead.

A crosswalk is a reading aid, not a compliance opinion. Neither the Canadian nor the UK
text maps one-to-one onto SR 11-7, and none of the three regulators has reviewed this
platform. A validator should check each row against the text it cites.

None of the three documents addresses AI agents used to *build* models; the last row maps
what they say about AI in models, and D10 explains how this documentation applies it.
